text: A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjaminite.[^shiggaion: a musical or literary term of uncertain meaning, perhaps an impassioned song.]

versions.text: A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjaminite.
versions.explanation: The transliterated term "shiggaion" will be opaque to listeners. A brief footnote explaining that it is a musical/literary term of uncertain meaning helps the reader without disturbing the oral flow of the superscription.

text: O LORD my God, in you I take refuge; save me from all who pursue me, and deliver me,
or he will seize me like a lion, ripping me to pieces with no one to rescue me.

versions.text: or he will tear me apart like a lion, dragging me off with no one to rescue me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two distinct verbs: יִטְרֹף (seize/prey upon) and פֹּרֵק (rend, tear in pieces). The current rendering puts the tearing first and reduces פֹּרֵק to "dragging me off," which loses the violent sense of rending. Reversing the images keeps both verbs' force and the natural build of the line.

text: O LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is guilt on my hands,
if I have repaid my friend with evil, or plundered my enemy without cause,
then let my enemy pursue me and overtake me; let him trample my life into the ground and lay my honor in the dust. Selah
Rise up, O LORD, in your anger; lift yourself against the fury of my foes. Awake for me; you have commanded judgment.
Let the assembly of the peoples gather around you, and over them return on high.

versions.text: Let the assembly of the peoples gather around you, and take your seat high above them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb שׁוּבָה means "return," picturing God ascending again to his exalted place; "take your seat" adds an image of enthronement not in the text. "Return on high" is both more literal and rhythmically strong at the end of the line.

text: The LORD judges the nations. Judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and the integrity that is in me.
Put an end to the malice of the wicked, and establish the righteous, you who test hearts and minds, O righteous God.
My shield is God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, a God who shows his wrath every day.
If a man does not repent, God sharpens his sword; he bends his bow and takes aim.
He has prepared his deadly weapons; he makes ready his flaming arrows.
See how the wicked man labors with evil; he conceives trouble and gives birth to lies.
He digs a pit and hollows it out, and falls into the hole he has made.
His trouble comes back on his own head; his violence comes down on the crown of his head.

versions.text: His trouble comes back on his own head; his violence falls on his own skull.
versions.explanation: קָדְקֹד means the crown or top of the head, not "skull," which carries a grimmer, anatomical connotation absent from the Hebrew. "Comes down" also better reflects יֵרֵד and gives the closing line a fuller cadence for reading aloud.

text: I will praise the LORD for his righteousness; I will sing to the name of the LORD Most High.
